candidates.title: Machine learning predicts intensive care mortality from the first six hours of vital signs
candidates.abstract: Early warning of clinical deterioration remains challenging in intensive care units. We developed a gradient boosted decision tree trained on the first six hours of vital signs and laboratory results from 42118 admissions to predict in-hospital mortality. In temporal validation the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86, compared with 0.74 for the conventional early warning score. External validation in two hospitals confirmed calibration. Our results suggest that machine learning applied to routine electronic health record data can identify high risk patients several hours before clinical deterioration.

candidates.title: Serum procalcitonin kinetics guide antibiotic stewardship in ventilator-associated pneumonia
candidates.abstract: Procalcitonin kinetics over the first three days of therapy were associated with shorter antibiotic courses in a retrospective cohort of 1,204 ventilator-associated pneumonia patients. A decline of at least thirty percent by day three identified patients who could safely stop antibiotics.

candidates.title: Biomarker panels for septic shock recognition in children: a multicenter prospective study
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric septic shock is difficult to recognize early. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 3,102 children across 18 emergency departments and compared a three-biomarker panel with single markers. RESULTS: The panel improved sensitivity from 0.71 to 0.84 without loss of specificity. CONCLUSIONS: A simple biomarker panel may support earlier recognition of pediatric septic shock.

candidates.title: Deep learning early warning for sepsis on general wards: a stepped cluster randomized implementation
candidates.abstract: Deploying a sepsis early warning model across 32 general wards reduced time to first antibiotic by 1.8 hours in a stepped cluster randomized trial. Alert acceptance by bedside nurses was 78 percent, and no increase in alert fatigue was observed over six months.
